title: Transparency in Federal Buildings Projects Act of 2019
official_summary:
Transparency in Federal Buildings Projects Act of 2019

This bill requires the General Services Administration (GSA) to make available to the public on its website all prospectuses submitted by the GSA to Congress concerning certain proposed public building projects and associated information, subject to requirements that (1) the GSA maintain the information so that it is easily accessible and downloadable; (2) the information is kept current and the prospectuses and associated information are updated regularly; and (3) the information required by this bill be inclusive for at least 10 years.

summary.headline: A 2021 law requires the General Services Administration to post public building project proposals sent to Congress on its website and keep them available for at least 10 years.
summary.what_it_does: The General Services Administration (GSA) must make public, on its website, the prospectuses it submits to Congress for certain proposed federal public building projects, along with related information. The information must be easy to find and download, kept current, and updated regularly. It must stay available for at least 10 years.

who_it_affects.how: Anyone can look up and download GSA's proposals for certain federal building projects instead of requesting them separately.
GSA must post these prospectuses and related details online, keep them updated, and maintain them for at least 10 years.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress and their staff
who_it_affects.how: The GSA project proposals they receive are also published on a public website, so the public can see the same documents.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 13, 2021. The summary does not state a separate start date for the website requirements.
